memoryText: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Psalm 119:105 slowly, several times, and then say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
This is one of the best-loved verses about Scripture, from the middle of the longest chapter in the Bible. It uses a simple image: a lamp.

“Your word.” The psalmist speaks to God, and says that the word is his. It is not the opinion of men. It is God’s speech, and it has his authority and his love in it.

“Is a lamp to my feet.” In the ancient world, a lamp was a small oil flame, held at the level of the feet. It did not light up the whole road. It showed the next few steps. This is how God’s word usually works. We do not get a complete map of our future. We get enough light for the next step. And the psalmist does not complain about it. He is grateful for it. We walk by faith, one step at a time.

“And a light to my path.” The path is the whole road of life, and the word shows where it leads. “Path” also suggests direction. The word of God not only lights each step but also reveals where it all goes, and warns of where the other paths end.

The verse invites us to treat the Bible not as a book of general ideas but as a daily guide. When you are unsure of a decision, the lamp is for your feet. When you are tempted, the lamp shows the pit. When you are afraid of the future, the lamp reminds you that the one who holds it knows the way.

For the Christian, this verse is fulfilled in Christ, who said, “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life” (John 8:12). The word that lights our path has a name. Walk in his light.
weekInReview: This week you worked through the heart of Proverbs. You read the two banquets of Wisdom and Folly, and the first collection of Solomon’s sayings, with their contrasts between the righteous and the wicked. You saw how the gentle answer turns away wrath, how the tongue holds the power of life and death, and how the name of the LORD is a strong tower. You saw that human plans are held in God’s hand: the heart of man plans his way, but the LORD establishes his steps, and the king’s heart is a stream of water in his hand. In Psalm 119 you heard the psalmist turn to God’s word in affliction and say that it is good that he was afflicted. The week taught that wisdom is practical, that God is sovereign over human plans, and that his word is a light for each step.
reflectionQuestions: Proverbs says that the name of the LORD is a strong tower, and that a rich man’s wealth is a strong city only in his imagination. What do you run to when you feel unsafe, and is it a real tower?
Jesus is the friend who sticks closer than a brother, and the one who held fast to the Father’s will. How does knowing his friendship change how you face a lonely or hard moment this week?
Psalm 119:105 says God’s word is a lamp to the feet. What is the next step you need light for, and how will you ask God for it?
prayerPrompts: Thank God that his word is a lamp for your feet.
Thank him for the strong tower of his name.
Rest, and ask him to establish your steps.
